candidates.cite: by The British Library; No restrictions; https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Plan_of_Raby_Castle_(1897).jpg
candidates.place_reason: 306e audit 2026-10-13: similarity (4 pts, resid 0.0 m, 0.67 m/px, 0.0 deg) - the 4 anchors are the plate's 900-px corners, a ladder with no placement information: the fit pins the plate centre onto the site point. The drawing is an idealised 1897 castle complex spanning the whole 600 m fit box (the 1280x1080 plate = 853 x 720 m on the ground): Great Keep, Great Hall, Gate House, Main Street, Market Cross, St Mary's, North/South Towers. The real Raby Castle (1842 six-inch + LiDAR) is a small ~50 m ruin on a ~90 m round terrace with a moat, centred on the site point just north of Low Pond; the drawn Gate House (E-139 N-214), St Mary's (E-93 N+45) and N Tower (E+34 N+281) all sit on open park. Wrong size (~10x), the drawn works miss the real ones. Document deleted.
